exercise.name: Dumbbell Lying One Arm Rear Lateral Raise

reference.title: Dumbbell Lying One Arm Rear Lateral Raise
reference.listing: Page not read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the arm rises, breathe in as it lowers.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.progression: Add reps, then weight; pause at the top

cues.text: Lie on your left side, knees bent, head resting on the left arm. Hold the dumbbell in the right hand in front of the chest, arm long with a soft elbow, palm facing you and thumb toward your head.
Breathe out and sweep the straight arm up and back until it points at the ceiling; lead with the back of the hand.
Arm vertical over the shoulder; squeeze the shoulder blade back.
Breathe in and lower slowly to in front of the chest.
Hover just above the floor and repeat. Then switch sides.

mistakes.mistake: Rolling the trunk back to swing the weight up
mistakes.fix: Stay stacked on your side; only the arm moves.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the elbow into a row
mistakes.fix: Keep the arm long with a fixed soft elbow.
Stop with the arm pointing at the ceiling.

kinematics.norm: From in front of the chest to vertical, about 90 degrees of sweep (clinical opinion); prone horizontal abduction gave high posterior deltoid EMG (Reinold 2007)
Neutral, thumb toward the head throughout; a neutral grip gave more posterior deltoid activity than a pronated one in a horizontal abduction exercise (Schoenfeld 2013)
Side-lying, knees bent, head on the lower arm (clinical opinion)
Controlled, short pause at the top (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #5043, Dumbbell Lying One Arm Rear Lateral Raise, video (movement reference only; page not read)
Reinold et al. 2007, electromyographic analysis of the supraspinatus and deltoid muscles during 3 common rehabilitation exercises (J Athl Train 42(4):464-469)
Schoenfeld et al. 2013, effect of hand position on EMG activity of the posterior shoulder musculature during a horizontal abduction exercise (J Strength Cond Res 27(10):2644-2649)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Stay stacked on your side so the low back does not twist.
modify: Shoulder pinching at the top: stop a little before vertical.
Bottom shoulder uncomfortable: put a pillow under the head.

muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Prime mover: lifts the arm up and back (horizontal abduction), loaded most when the arm is near horizontal.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Draw the shoulder blade back at the top.
